content: The risk of adverse effects may increase if you are using certain medications, such as diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), or if you have medical conditions that lead to significant fluid loss, such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Clarithromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, rendering them less effective. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if it is absolutely necessary, as determined by your healthcare provider. Additionally, clarithromycin is known to pass into breast milk, which may have implications for nursing infants. Drug interactions can alter the way your medications work or increase the likelihood of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a comprehensive list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the elimination of clarithromycin from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Conversely, clarithromycin can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, which may impact their function. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For less urgent cases, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as cultures or liver and kidney function tests, to monitor your response to treatment. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Clarithromycin is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It may also be used in combination with anti-ulcer medications to treat certain types of stomach ulcers or to prevent specific bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as macrolide antibiotics. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually every 12 hours. For optimal effectiveness, take it at evenly spaced intervals. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in a recurrence of the infection. If you are taking this medication to prevent certain bacterial infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor. Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, and changes in taste. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking clarithromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin or azithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Clarithromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be further elevated if you are using certain medications, such as diuretics, or if you have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Clarithromycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as determined by your healthcare provider. It is also known to pass into breast milk, which may have implications for nursing infants.
